doc.title: Wayne Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

chapter: Manhattan School and the Benny Goodman Russian tour
title: Teddy Wilson and how Goodman got Andre released from CBS
summary: Teddy Wilson hardly played; Goodman reportedly went to Paley to free Andre to replace Knepper.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Well yeah. I don’t think there’s anybody in the band that was certainly — you know ironically if anybody in that band, and I’m thinking about everybody in the band now, if anybody had something nice to say about Benny and not dark and negative, it was Teddy Wilson. Teddy Wilson wasn’t getting to play at all and — hardly at all — and he was as mild in manner, he was a gentleman. I mean this is like, Teddy Wilson was a first class cat man. And I don’t know, there are certain things that could have been better on the part of the musicians themselves. It became like — in a way it became a little bit like a revolution going on too. Well let’s start the ball going. Okay? I had, first of all, I wasn’t initially supposed to go at all. Jimmy Knepper got the mumps and he couldn’t go to the World’s Fair and to Seattle. That was the first gig first, because of the mumps. And so Benny called Lou Schoobe who was the contractor at CBS to find out if I could get a break from the Gary Moore Show and Schoobe said no, I couldn’t go. Or maybe he called me and I asked, I can’t remember all that. So Benny, well I mean it’s a feather in © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-

my cap I guess but this is what was told to me, I mean it was told to me by the contractor at CBS, not by Benny, that Benny went to Paley, William Paley. He went to the CEO, and said I want this guy and tell the contractor to let him go. So I mean it makes me feel good that somebody wanted me that much to go through all that trouble. And so that made me feel good. So from that standpoint it’s hard to badmouth someone — but anyways, so I went. And some kid that was playing third trombone, he was a teacher and I don’t know how he got hooked up with the Benny thing and everything else, but we went out to Seattle and the World’s Fair and everything else. We came back to New York and Jimmy Knepper re-joined the band. And this kid left. Instead of me going, this kid left. I stayed on the band. So I forget — what was the question relating to this? Was there? I just can’t remember.
